prompt: How do I use breakout rooms in Teams?
completion:
**Using Breakout Rooms in Microsoft Teams** Breakout rooms let you split a Teams meeting into smaller groups so participants can work in parallel. Below is a quick‑start guide that covers the most common scenarios (desktop, web, and mobile) and a few best‑practice tips. --- ## 1. Prerequisites | Item | Why it matters | How to check / enable | |------|----------------|-----------------------| | **Breakout rooms are allowed in your policy** | Admins can disable them. | Teams Admin Center → **Teams** → **Meetings** → **Meeting policies** → *Choose policy* → **Breakout rooms** = *Allowed* | | **You are the meeting organizer or host** | Only the host can create or manage rooms. | The meeting creator or someone who has been granted *Presenter* role. | | **Teams is up to date** | Older clients may lack the UI. | Windows/macOS app → *Help* → *Check for updates*; Web → use a modern browser (Edge, Chrome, Firefox). | | **Meeting is a scheduled Teams meeting or channel meeting** | Breakout rooms are not available in ad‑hoc calls or regular Teams calls on mobile (though mobile hosts can join a room). | Schedule in Calendar or in a channel → **New meeting**. | --- ## 2. Create Breakout Rooms (During the Meeting) > **Tip:** You can set up rooms *before* the meeting starts, or while the meeting is live. The UI is the same. 1. **Join the meeting** as the host. 2. In the meeting toolbar, click **More actions** (…) → **Breakout rooms** (desktop) or tap the **Breakout rooms** icon (mobile). 3. Choose how many rooms you want (1‑30). - *If you want the same number of rooms as participants*, you can let Teams auto‑assign them later. 4. Click **Create rooms**. - Teams will create blank rooms with default names (Room 1, Room 2, …). --- ## 3. Assign Participants You can assign participants **before** or **after** creating rooms. | Assignment method | When to use it | Steps | |-------------------|----------------|-------| | **Automatically** (random or balanced) | Quick setup, no manual grouping needed | After creating rooms, click **Assign automatically**. Teams will distribute participants evenly. | | **Manually** | You have specific groups or need control | • After creating rooms, click **Assign manually**.
• Drag participants from the **Available participants** list into each room. | | **Pre‑assigned** | Rooms were set up ahead of time (e.g., via a spreadsheet) | Use the **Upload groups** feature (if available) or do it manually. | > **Note:** > - Participants will see a pop‑up invitation *“You have been added to Room X”*. > - They can **request to join the host’s room** if they need to. --- ## 4. Managing Rooms While They’re Live | Action | What it does | How to do it | |--------|--------------|--------------| | **Move participants to another room** | Host can shuffle people on the fly | In the breakout‑room window, click **Move** next to a participant, then select the target room. | | **Join a room yourself** | Host can enter any room | Click **Join room** next to the desired room. | | **Close all rooms** | Ends the breakout experience and returns everyone to the main meeting | Click **Close all rooms**. The host gets a countdown (default 60 s) before everyone is brought back. | | **Reopen or re‑create rooms** | If you need to start over | Click **Create rooms** again (you’ll be prompted to close existing rooms first). | | **Add or remove participants after creation** | You can adjust groupings on the fly | In the breakout‑room window, click **Add participants** or **Remove** next to a room. | --- ## 5. Recording Breakout Rooms (Optional) 1. **Record from the main meeting**: The recording will include all rooms automatically (the host’s recording will capture what happens in each room). 2. **Record each room separately**: The host can start a recording *within* a breakout room. - In the room, click **More actions** (…) → **Start recording**. - When finished, click **Stop recording**. - Each room’s recording will be saved separately in OneDrive/SharePoint. > **Tip:** Let participants know when a recording starts; Teams shows a banner at the top of the room. --- ## 6. After the Meeting - **Download recordings**: Go to the meeting chat → **Files** → look for *Teams Meeting – – *. - **Export transcripts**: If you had *Transcription* enabled, you can download the transcript file from the same location. - **Review breakout‑room chats**: Each room has its own chat thread in the meeting’s chat section. --- ## 7. Common Troubleshooting | Symptom | Likely cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | Breakout rooms button missing | Policy disabled or outdated Teams client | Verify policy in Admin Center; update the app. | | Participants can’t see the “Join room” button | They’re not presenters or don’t have permission | Host can promote them to *Presenter* or add them as *Attendee* with “Allow to present” turned on. | | Rooms not auto‑assigning | “Assign automatically” not enabled | Click **Assign automatically** after room creation. | | Mobile host can’t create rooms | Mobile hosts can’t create rooms, only join | Use the desktop or web client for host duties. | --- ## 8. Quick Reference Cheat Sheet | Action | Desktop Shortcut | Web Shortcut | Mobile | |--------|------------------|--------------|--------| | Create rooms | `...` → **Breakout rooms** | Same | Tap **More** → **Breakout rooms** | | Assign participants | **Assign automatically** / **Assign manually** | Same | Same | | Join a room | **Join room** | Same | Same | | Close all rooms | **Close all rooms** | Same | Same | | Move participant | **Move** next to name | Same | Same | | Record in room | **Start recording** in room | Same | Same | --- ### Final Tips for a Smooth Breakout Experience 1. **Plan room numbers** – don’t create more rooms than you have participants; otherwise, some rooms will stay empty. 2. **Use clear room names** – especially if you’ll assign participants manually (e.g., “Project A – Design”). 3. **Test ahead** – schedule a test meeting with a few teammates to make sure everything works in your environment. 4. **Use the breakout‑room chat** for quick questions; it’s separate from the main meeting chat. 5. **Inform participants** that they can request to join the host’s room if they need help. With these steps, you’ll be able to set up, manage, and wrap up breakout rooms in Teams like a pro. Happy collaborating!
